passages.original: Γράμματα, ἔφη, καὶ τῶν ἄλλων μαθημάτων ἃ καὶ Πλάτων φησὶν ὡσανεὶ χαλινοῦ τινος δύναμιν ἔχειν τοῖς νέοις, ἵνα μὴ εἰς ἕτερα περισπῶνται.
passages.english: "Letters," he said, "and those of the other studies which, as Plato too says, have for the young the power, as it were, of a kind of bridle, so that they may not be drawn away to other things."
passages.notes: The sentence is elliptical: it answers a question from the surrounding dialogue (apparently what certain learning consists of), so the main verb is understood. The genitive τῶν ἄλλων μαθημάτων is read as partitive with the relative ἃ ("those of the other studies which").
